ruling.recommended_action: Close file: the detour is exempt under RD-4(a) (breakdown on the optimal route) and also consented to under RD-5. Explain to the rider that the extra kilometres are metered RydeTAXI fare; no refund and no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: I read the chat (2 timestamped messages, both about route choice), the rider's complaint (a longer-route/fare complaint only) and the driver's post-trip statement. Nothing contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so this is not a SAFE-1/SAFE-2 case.

Merits: the only off-route segment is F3 (10:13-10:24, 7.21 km driven vs 2.29 km optimal, +4.92 km, max 1794 m off route). This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the meter makes extra kilometres part of the fare (policy sec.0) and the case turns on whether the segment is exempt.

RD-4(a): the driver's claim of a breakdown (F11) is corroborated. F15 records a Vehicle breakdown on the Ayer Rajah Expressway (towards Tuas), reported 09:47, located 0 m from the optimal route - inside the 300 m matching radius, reported before the segment began and still active during it. F12 adds an AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY speed band 2 (10-19 km/h) covering 09:45-10:13. The cause hits the displaced stretch of the optimal route, so the segment is exempt: no_action on that basis. The chat messages speak of "traffic building up" (F8/F9) rather than a breakdown, but the exemption rests on F15, not on the driver's wording.

RD-5 independently: the consent message was sent before the detour began (F9 at 10:10 vs F3 starting 10:13), from the rider's own account, and "Sure, your call." is an express authorisation of the driver's proposed route via Clementi Avenue 2 - a general route authorisation for reaching the destination, which is what the segment is. Considered objection: no record ties the 10:13-10:24 segment to Clementi Avenue 2 (the file gives a start time but no road name for the segment, G13); on that reading the segment would be undetermined and would go to a human. That reading is not needed here because RD-4(a) already settles the segment on a system record.

Amount: with the segment exempt, no extra_km is refundable under RD-2, so the refundable amount is $0 and the ruling is no_action, with no RD-1 breach recorded. All billed items are published RydeTAXI components - distance/time on the meter, waiting $0.13 (0.5 min x $0.26/min; RD-3(c), F5) and platform $1.47 (F7). F4's "$7.99 excess distance" (5.67 km x $1.4099/km) is simply the metered cost of the kilometres driven, not a separate overcharge, and nothing unbilled appears (FARE-1).

Account flag: RD-6 needs a refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach, and F18 shows 0 upheld route disputes - neither condition is met, so no flag.

Evidence status: sufficient. GPS covers the trip and the segment (F1-F3), every chat message is timestamped (F10), the traffic incident feed is present (F12, F15) and the fare breakdown is complete (F4-F7).

segment_findings.reason: RD-4(a): a Vehicle breakdown (F15, reported 09:47, 0 m from the optimal route i.e. inside the 300 m radius, before the 10:13 segment start and active through it) plus a speed band 2 (10-19 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway covering 09:45-10:13 (F12) corroborate a reasonable cause on the displaced stretch of the optimal route; the segment is exempt. Independently under RD-5, the rider's own message sent at 10:10, before the segment started at 10:13, "Sure, your call." (F9), answering the driver's proposal to go round via Clementi Avenue 2 (F8), is prior express consent to the route change (general route authorisation); no record ties the segment to a named road, but the traffic record already settles it.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider's claim that the longer way round was unjustified and the 7.99 difference (F4) should be refunded: the only off-route segment (F3) is exempt under RD-4(a) - the Ayer Rajah Expressway breakdown in F15 sits on the optimal route - and was also consented to in advance (F9 vs the 10:13 start of F3) under RD-5, so RD-2 yields 0 refundable and no RD-1 breach is recorded.

Driver's post-trip assertion that the whole road was slow and he took another way is not relied on, and is not treated as proof of verbal consent: RD-5 consent is established from the rider's own timestamped message (F9), not from the driver's statement (F11).
